structuredIncident.summary: The R3 exit carrier beam fell from the yoke into the mill pit at approximately 1:03 PM on October 14, 2024 (Turn 2). The incident occurred during an outage preparation phase where work rolls and backup rolls had been removed. Key contextual facts include that the top backup roll balance was left isolated in a raised position and B hydraulics were shut off/bled prior to this shift. Two witnesses observed the fall; no personnel were in the pit at the time of impact, though contractors worked there earlier. The beam assembly (beam + link) landed intact with the keeper still installed.
structuredIncident.focalEvent: R3 exit carrier beam falls from yoke into mill pit
structuredIncident.actualImpact: Falling object incident; potential for severe injury or death if personnel had been present in the impact zone. No injuries reported at time of event, but area was red-flagged and investigation initiated.
structuredIncident.potentialImpact: Severe physical trauma to any person located within the fall path (mill pit) during the outage window.

structuredIncident.eventState: Outage preparation: work rolls and top/bottom backup rolls removed from R3 stand. Top backup roll balance left isolated/raised. B hydraulics shut off and bled. Carrier beam unsecured/fallen into pit.

evidenceClaims.text: The R3 exit carrier beam fell from the yoke into the mill pit at approximately 1:03 PM on October 14, 2024.
Work rolls and top/bottom backup rolls were removed from the R3 stand prior to the incident.
The top backup roll balance was left isolated in a raised position after roll removal.
B hydraulics were shut off and bled prior to the incident.
Contractor employees worked in the mill pit throughout the morning of Turn 2.
No personnel were in the mill pit at the time of impact.
The beam assembly (beam + link) landed intact with the keeper still installed.
Two witnesses observed the fall.
The 'keeper' reported as installed was functional and correctly seated prior to fall.
B hydraulics provided active support or tensioning that was released upon isolation/bleeding.
A formal energy isolation verification was completed before leaving the area unattended.
The mechanism by which the beam detached from the yoke (e.g., loss of keeper function, structural failure).
The specific configuration of the top backup roll balance in its isolated/raised state and how that relates to beam retention geometry.
The 'keeper' device was reported as still installed on the recovered assembly.
The top backup roll balance was left isolated in a raised position prior to the incident.
B hydraulics system was shut off and bled before the shift change/turn.
No formal energy isolation verification record has been located to confirm the safe state of the raised balance and bled hydraulics before personnel left the area.
Contractor employees worked in the mill pit throughout the morning of October 14, 2024.
The sequence of tasks performed between previous shift turnover and 1:03 PM (who did what, when) is unknown.
Whether a formal energy isolation verification was completed before leaving the area unattended is unknown and requires record review.
The specific mechanical interaction between the raised top backup roll balance and carrier beam retention geometry has not been established without engineering drawings.
Whether B hydraulics provided active support or tensioning that was released upon isolation/bleeding is unknown without circuit diagrams.
The current status of work orders, permits, or stop-work authorizations active at the time of the event is unknown.
The mechanism by which the beam detached from the yoke (e.g., keeper failure, structural fatigue, misalignment) is currently unknown.
The functional status and seating verification of the 'keeper' prior to fall remains unconfirmed.

nodes.label: Top backup roll balance left isolated in a raised position.
nodes.detail: The top backup roll balance was removed from its operational state and positioned vertically (raised) prior to the incident. This altered the mechanical configuration of the stand area.

nodes.label: B hydraulics system shut off and bled.
nodes.detail: The B hydraulic circuit was isolated (shut off) and depressurized (bled) before the incident occurred. This action removed active pressure from a specific subsystem.

nodes.label: R3 exit carrier beam falls from yoke into mill pit.
nodes.detail: The heavy load detached and fell approximately 1:03 PM on October 14, 2024. No injuries occurred as the area was clear at impact.

nodes.detail: Personnel were present and working in the impact zone prior to the fall, establishing a hazard scenario before the event.

edges.rationale: The raised balance altered the mechanical geometry or load path, potentially compromising the keeper's ability to retain the beam when other supports were removed.
edges.counterfactual: If the balance had remained in its operational (lowered) position during roll removal and hydraulic bleeding, would the beam have retained?
edges.competingExplanation: The fall was caused by a catastrophic failure of the keeper mechanism unrelated to geometry changes.
edges.evidenceGap: Engineering drawings are required to verify if the raised configuration physically interferes with or unloads the keeper.

edges.rationale: Bleeding the hydraulics may have released stored energy or removed active support/tensioning that was stabilizing the beam assembly.
edges.counterfactual: If B hydraulics were not supporting any load path, bleeding them would be neutral.
edges.competingExplanation: The fall occurred due to a mechanical defect in the keeper unrelated to hydraulic pressure changes.
edges.evidenceGap: Circuit diagrams are needed to confirm if 'B' system provided active support or tensioning for the beam assembly.

edges.rationale: Removing work rolls and backup rolls eliminated primary structural support, leaving the beam dependent solely on the keeper or secondary supports which may have been compromised by other conditions.
edges.counterfactual: If work rolls remained installed during hydraulic bleeding/roll removal tasks, would the fall have occurred?
edges.competingExplanation: The beam fell due to a sudden structural failure of the yoke itself rather than loss of support.
edges.evidenceGap: Inspection records or engineering analysis required to confirm if roll removal was part of standard procedure that inherently leaves the beam unsecured until reinstalled.

edges.rationale: Lack of verification that the system was in a safe state (zero energy, secure geometry) before leaving it unattended allowed an unsafe condition to persist into Turn 2.
edges.counterfactual: If formal LOTO verification had been completed and documented prior to shift change, would the fall have occurred?
edges.competingExplanation: The incident was caused by a latent equipment defect that existed regardless of procedural compliance.
edges.evidenceGap: Shift logs or turnover notes are needed to confirm if verification steps were skipped due to oversight rather than absence of records.

edges.rationale: The keeper device failed to prevent the fall. This failure could be due to improper seating caused by geometry changes, mechanical fatigue, or a design flaw.
edges.counterfactual: If the keeper had been functional and correctly seated prior to detachment, would it have prevented the beam from falling?
edges.competingExplanation: The fall was caused by external impact (e.g., vibration) rather than barrier failure.
edges.evidenceGap: Physical inspection of the recovered keeper is required to determine if it failed due to seating issues or material fatigue.
